plain: A hint that suggests something without saying it outright

webster.text: The act of insinuating; a creeping or winding in; a flowing into crevices.

more.text: The act of gaining on favor or affections, by gentle or artful means.
The art or power of pleasing and stealing on the affections.
A hint; a suggestion or intimation by distant allusion.

example.quote: It has been said that some might contemplate disunion without terror. 1 have heard no sentiment from any gentleman that can warrant such an insinuation.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, June 23, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
